treatment: Dramatist winner with grafts, restaged at Gate 0. CHALKY, a dented safety-orange surveyor's chalk-line reel in an olive knit earflap hat, snaps a dashed ultramarine chalk line across the Tanana valley snow in the clear mint afterglow of a Fairbanks winter afternoon; its far end runs into a bank of ice fog (loop 1). A faceless figure tagged MAYOR GRIER HOPKINS pinches a chalk mark at 12 on the line, and the commission row pulls six more feet off the spool and marks 18 inside a dashed RECOMMENDED border. A cutaway inside the reel shows three trip pins under PROPOSED THRESHOLDS, each tripped by a dashed hypothetical block outline, a dashed RECOMMENDED flag popping, the line never clamping a building. One GVEA wire carries a spring-green pulse into a dashed 5 MW outline and the valley's windows light to AT LEAST 3,000 HOMES while Earl, a faceless plugged-in pickup, shivers in the lot (only here and at the button). The map floods sage across 97 of 100 squares; a parka figure tagged ANY BUILDER reads the line and wonders when it turns to paint (loop 2). Chalky walks the line under the wire into fog; hard cut to the Eielson chain-link (rust-brown wire, nothing behind it but snow and spruce): the chalk stops at the OUTSIDE of the wire, piles gray there and the line goes slack. Hedged cards hang on the wire; a gray swatch with blank black and white halves. Act 3, THE FAIR TEST: three named reasons for time each tie a rope that LIFTS the slack line, Chalky pulling with them (a commissioner with a diesel genset icon on the rope tag, another commissioner hearing anxiety over AI in general, a resident), then the opposite view gets the same physical language, the line past month 10 lying on the snow as a long unheld slack coil, THE EXTRA 8 MONTHS, NEITHER OUTLET SAYS WHY, and the builder picks up its end. At the borough building a frosted stopwatch hangs at zero by NOT LAW YET with two sealed paint cans at its foot; a dashed ghost hand previews the sweep the vote would start. Chalky reels in through the fog: the end comes out bare and frayed, and two dashed chalk marks wait on the snow to be struck, RULES A BUILDER CAN MEET and AN ANSWER AT THE FENCE. The camera cranes up for the signature: the line crisp across the valley, slack and gray at the outside of the far chain-link, Earl still shivering, and Chalky re-snaps it.

palette.sky: #BFE3D2 mint afterglow at the horizon rising through #7DB7AE sea-glass to #3E6E78 deep teal overhead; NO sun disc (the sun is already behind the Alaska Range at 2 p.m.), so light is skylight, soft and clear
palette.ground: #EEEAF4 lilac-white snow with #B9A9C9 mauve skylight shade (short, soft, under objects, not raking); the Chena a frozen pearl ribbon #E6E3EA with a dark spruce bank, never a blue stroke
palette.fog: #E4E2EA ice fog ONLY at the Eielson fence and the line's far end
palette.spruce: #22433A spruce with #4C6E5E lit tips and snow loads
palette.hero: #E8582A safety-orange reel, #9C3418 shade, #FFC9A8 rim on the key side; brass #C9A04A crank and hook; moss knit hat #5E7A3A with #EEEAF4 fleece
palette.line: #2F5FD0 surveyor's ultramarine chalk, the ONLY high-chroma blue in the film; nothing else (hat, river, outlines, plate borders, block outlines) is blue
palette.gray_area: #8F9096 neutral gray, the ONLY true neutral, on the chalk piled at the outside of the wire and the swatch
palette.fence: #6B4A36 weathered umber-brown wire and posts (L* 33), so the gray reads against it
palette.flood: #A9BE9A dusty sage for the general-use zone (L* 75), the ultramarine line (L* 42) reads on it at stroke width
palette.grid: #3FCB73 spring green, ONLY a travelling pulse on the GVEA wire, never an arrival flash or glow at the dashed 5 MW outline (it must read as power flowing, never as a green light); windows light a warm cream #FFE9B0 as ordinary houses do
palette.cans: #16181D charcoal and #F7F7F2 white, lids always sealed
palette.metals: stopwatch #B8743A copper case with a frosted face, genset icon #C98A2E ochre, H-frame poles #7A5A3C wood, Earl's pickup #7A2E3A maroon
palette.plate: #FFF6E3 cream plates with #1B1A22 type; RECOMMENDED borders dashed in ink, never chalk blue
palette.mood: clear, bright, cold air you can see, curious and a little comic, never doomy
palette.divergence: 11-16 was indigo polar night and midnight-sun honey over rust tundra with radar lime; 11-15 rain-black night under a sodium lamp with gunmetal and pencilled vellum; 11-12 a rose-line dusk dome with a survey stake and a raven; 11-11 a pink-gold ice-fog noon in Fairbanks. This film is a clear mint-afterglow afternoon with NO sun, lilac snow, sage, rust-brown wire and one ultramarine chalk line; fog appears only at the fence. The hero's safety orange is pushed away from 11-16's thermometer red.

light.time: Fairbanks mid-November about 3 p.m., minutes before sunset: the low sun is occluded by the Alaska Range to the south, the sky glows mint above the ridge, and the valley is lit by clear skylight
light.key: broad soft skylight from above and slightly left (the bright horizon at screen left), so forms shade gently to the right and down; no long shadows, contact shadows under everything
light.rim: a cool mint rim #DFF3EA on the left edges against the deep teal upper sky
light.arc: Act 1 clear and bright; Act 2 the fog thickens and the key desaturates as the line nears the fence (S8, S9); Act 3 flat and even under the ropes (S10 to S13); Act 4 the fog thins and the clear afterglow returns for the reel-in and the crane-up (S15, S16)

light.depth: three planes: far Alaska Range silhouette under the mint glow, mid valley with spruce ranks and the line, near plane snow drifts, plug-in posts and spruce trunks in y 1480 to 1920; parallax on every exterior; fog density rises with distance only near the fence

shape_language: Chalky is ROUND and compact (a fat disc case, stubby crank, mitten boots); this is the third rounded hero in a row (VoteTree, Flap, Chalky), and the contrast lives between him and the line, the one STRAIGHT taut vector in the film. The world is soft (drifts, spruce loads, fog); the fence is a rigid rust-brown diamond lattice; slack line is a sagging curve, so taut and slack read muted. Cans are squat sealed cylinders.

casting.hero: Chalky (NET-NEW, lib/chalkline.tsx): a faced surveyor's chalk-line reel with crank arm, moss knit earflap hat, brass hook, and `cues` beat poses. The ONLY face in the film.
casting.net_new_supporting: ChalkLine (dashed snapped string, ultramarine with a gray slack end, sag and fade), ChalkPuff, TripPinCutaway (labels engraved as each pin trips), PaintCan (sealed), ChalkMark (an unstruck dashed mark on the snow), Genset (faceless icon for a rope tag), ChainFence (rust-brown), all lib/chalkline.tsx.
casting.shelf: Pickup (lib/polecam.tsx) as Earl, faceless, a 2 px shiver and a sagging cord; Moose (fauna.tsx); Cable (lib/refinery.tsx) for the GVEA wire with a green pulse; Snowfall; IdleFigure + FigureFinish for every faceless parka figure.
casting.people: Mayor, commissioners, builder and resident are faceless parka figures with tags (MAYOR GRIER HOPKINS, PLANNING COMMISSION, A COMMISSIONER, ANY BUILDER, A RESIDENT); never faced, never caricatured.
casting.props: chalk marks on the line (episode), clothes peg and source slip (episode), dashed block outlines (episode), H-frame poles (Cable), hot dog cart and outhouse (episode), chain-link (ChainFence), newspaper page (episode), month strip and marker flags (episode), frosted stopwatch and borough building (episode), plug-in posts (episode)
casting.shelf_check: grep of video-engine/src/lib: no chain-link fence (10-23's fence was a rail fence inside an episode), no rope, no stopwatch on the shelf, so ChainFence is net-new; Cable (refinery) carries the wire pulse; Pickup (polecam) is Earl

motion_language: The snap is the hero move: a whip of the string with a travelling wave, a chalk puff on contact, dashes landing left to right. Chalky anticipates every crank, squashes on landing, breathes, and his earflaps follow through; he performs on his beats (cues). Taut versus slack is the film's motion argument: ropes LIFT the slack line with an ease, never a spring. Fog drifts on two speeds near the fence; snow sifts; the green pulse travels the wire; Earl shivers 2 px under 0.4 rad a frame.

composition.signature_shot: S16, beats 45 and 46, 113.22 to 117.92 s: the camera cranes up and back from Chalky to a high oblique of the Tanana valley in clear mint afterglow, the ultramarine dashed line crisp across the snow, going slack and gray at the outside of the umber Eielson chain-link far off, Earl still shivering in his lot in the near plane, and Chalky re-snapping the line.

practicals: Nothing is drawn inside the Eielson fence except snow and spruce; the chalk stops at the outside face of the wire; no guard tower. The line is always dashed chalk; every pause label says RECOMMENDED, PROPOSED or NOT LAW YET; no tick, no stamp of any kind, no APPROVED. The cans never open. The stopwatch's real hand stays at zero; only a dashed ghost previews a sweep. The extra 8 months carries NEITHER OUTLET SAYS WHY only. Ropes lift the slack line and Chalky pulls with them; every rope has an owner; at the reel-in the ropes stay knotted and wind onto the spool with the line. The pins trip dashed hypothetical outlines and pop RECOMMENDED flags, never clamp a building. Earl keeps shivering at the end. AI appears only as NOT A VOTE ON AI and the commissioner's quote. Hopkins's cards carry BELIEVES and MIGHT. Chalky is the only face.
craft_advance: none beyond the net-new chalkline family this film needs
